senses.definition: A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, family Apiaceae, especially the subspecies sativus.

quotes.text: In general, beets, carrots, and turnips are all of aphrodisiac value in erotic dietary.
quotes.reference: 1961, Harry E. Wedeck, Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs, New York: The Citadel Press, page 42:

senses.definition: A shade of orange similar to the flesh of most carrots (also called carrot orange).
(figurative) Any motivational tool; an incentive to do something.

quotes.text: Essentially, lawmakers replaced the sticks with carrots.
quotes.reference: 2022 August 7, Coral Davenport, Lisa Friedman, “Five Decades in the Making: Why It Took Congress So Long to Act on Climate”, in The New York Times, →ISSN:

quotes.text: In 2022, when the Biden administration finally succeeded in passing a major climate bill, it consisted almost entirely of carrots—tax credits and subsidies for green energy.
quotes.reference: 2023 August 7, Paul Krugman, “Climate Is Now a Culture War Issue”, in The New York Times:

senses.definition: (UK, slang, derogatory) Someone from a rural background.
(UK, slang) A police officer from somewhere within the British Isles, but specifically outside of Greater London.
(transitive) To treat (an animal pelt) with a solution of mercuric nitrate as part of felt manufacture.
